articles.title: What is the Budget and what could be in it?
articles.summary: Chancellor John Healey will set out his plans for UK taxes in October.
articles.body:
Chancellor John Healey will set out Labour's tax and spending plans when he delivers his first Budget on 28 October.

He has refused to rule out tax increases after acknowledging government borrowing costs are at "historic highs".

But the government's room for manoeuvre on tax is limited.

Before the 2024 general election, Labour promised not to increase three big revenue earners for the government: income tax, National Insurance and VAT.

In his statement, delivered to MPs in the House of Commons, Healey will set out how the government plans to raise or lower taxes.

Alongside the Budget, the Treasury will publish details about the measures and their costs.

The independent Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR), which monitors government spending, will also publish an assessment of the health of the UK economy and a forecast of what it thinks will happen in the future.

The run-up to the Budget typically sees speculation about what might be in it, which the government is trying to keep to a minimum this year.

Healey and Prime Minister Andy Burnham face a difficult balancing act, trying to offer more support to households and meet commitments on defence spending, while also sticking to Labour's manifesto commitments on tax and the government's self-imposed fiscal rules.

The previous chancellor, Rachel Reeves, set out two main rules, which the new leadership has vowed to follow. These are:

Not to borrow to fund day-to-day public spending by the end of this parliament

To get government debt falling as a share of national income by the end of this parliament

In March, the OBR calculated that the first rule would be met with a gap - or headroom - of £23.6bn. However, this headroom is expected to have shrunk.

Analysts at KPMG believe it could have fallen to £12bn, mainly due to the rise in government borrowing costs this year.

However, one option that has been floated is Healey potentially accepting a smaller buffer, reducing the need to increase taxes in the Budget.

Further details on the "Your First Home" scheme, aimed at helping first-time buyers in England to purchase a property, are expected to be announced in the Budget.

The scheme will allow people to buy a new-build home with a deposit of 2.5%. It would provide them with a loan worth 20% of their property's value to help pay for the purchase.

There has been speculation that Capital Gains Tax - which is imposed on the profit people make when they sell an asset that has increased in value - could be changed, through either higher rates or by removing or amending exemptions.

The High Value Council Tax Surcharge - dubbed the Mansion Tax - was announced in last year's Budget and will apply to properties in England valued above £2m from April 2028. However, reports have suggested the government is considering extending it to properties worth more than £1.5m.

Banks have been reporting bumper profits, leading to calls from unions to increase taxes on the sector . But banks have pushed back, suggesting heavier levies would undermine the government's aim to boost growth and make the UK less competitive.

Fuel duty was frozen under the Conservatives in March 2022 and Sir Keir Starmer's government continued the freeze, deciding in May to push back a planned 3p increase in September until the end of this year.

Healey told the BBC in late September that the "place" and "time" for dealing with rising petrol and diesel costs was the Budget, but would not give details on whether the freeze would be extended again.

In the first three months of the year, the UK's economy grew by 0.6%, although it slowed to 0.4% in the April-to-June period.

The Office for National Statistics said that figure was "relatively robust", with the UK growing faster than other G7 countries.

The most recent data showed the economy grew by 0.4% in July, which was much stronger than expected.

Analysts say the UK economy is proving resilient in the face of energy price shocks caused by the US-Israel war with Iran.

The conflict has led to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway for oil and gas trade. This caused a sharp jump in oil prices, which has fed through to higher energy and fuel prices.

Economists expect UK growth to slow in the months ahead as those costs continue to weigh on households and businesses.

Prices for goods and services are still rising faster than wanted. Inflation hit 3.1% in the year to August, the highest rate in five months, and above the Bank of England's 2% target, driven by higher petrol and diesel prices.

The Bank of England held interest rates at 3.75% for the sixth time in a row in September, but said they were likely to rise if high energy prices persist.

What time is the Budget and what happens afterwards?

The Budget speech usually starts at about 12:30 UK time - after Prime Minister's Questions - and lasts about an hour.

It will be broadcast live on the BBC iPlayer and on the BBC News website.

The Leader of the Opposition, Conservative MP Kemi Badenoch, will respond to the speech in the House of Commons.

MPs debate the measures for four days, before voting on them.

If approved by MPs, tax changes can come into effect immediately.

However, the government must pass a finance bill to make them permanent.

articles.title: 'Only one of 728 remains': Rahul's new charge against EC over Delhi's Bela Estate voter list
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Monday again targeted the Election Commission and CEC Gyanesh Kumar over the special intensive
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Monday again targeted the Election Commission and CEC Gyanesh Kumar over the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, citing the case of Delhi’s Bela Estate, where he claimed 727 of 728 names were removed from the voter list.Sharing a video of his phone call with the SDM over the SIR exercise on X, the Rae Bareli MP wrote, "728 people live in Bela Estate on the banks of the Yamuna. After SIR, only one name remains in the voter list - the other 727 names have been struck off."He said the residents had been living in the area for decades and had voted in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections and the 2025 Delhi assembly elections."In 2023, their homes were demolished - but they didn't go anywhere, they're still right here," Rahul said.Rahul said he visited the residents in their jhuggis and heard directly from them about what they alleged had happened during the SIR exercise.He said he also spoke to the SDM over the issue. "On the phone with the SDM, I said exactly this - having a house or not has no connection to the right to vote. CEC Gyanesh Kumar himself has said that "House Number 0" is for the homeless. Yet, 727 people's names have been struck off," he wrote.Former Congress president further criticised the SIR exercise, calling it "a method of vote theft" and alleging that it was taking away the only political power available to some of the country's poorest citizens.He also targeted chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar amid a controversy over an Indian Express report on alleged differences between the CEC and the other two election commissioners."Gyanesh Kumar will go. But the system that made him do this will also have to answer," Rahul said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Namibia spent decades building community conservancies; in 2026, a new plan aims to secure more than 20 million hectares
articles.summary: Namibia has secured a conservation financing agreement worth more than N$1 billion (approximately US$63 million) to support long-term community-based
articles.body: Namibia has secured a conservation financing agreement worth more than N$1 billion (approximately US$63 million) to support long-term community-based conservation in Namibia. The ‘Namibia for Life Project Finance for Permanence initiative’ was signed on 20 May 2026 in the presence of Prime Minister Dr Tjitunga Elijah Ngurare. According to the Joint Media Release, the agreement aims to secure conservation funding, policies and systems for more than 20 million hectares, covering over 20% of Namibia.It currently supports 87 communal conservancies and is expected to expand to as many as 100. More than 283,000 people who depend on wildlife and natural resources for their livelihoods are expected to benefit. The initiative also includes an endowment fund and a dedicated Socio-Economic Development Fund to provide longer-term support for conservation and communities.How will Namibia’s new conservation deal support more than 20 million hectaresThe ‘Namibia for Life Project Finance for Permanence initiative’ was signed on 20 May 2026 as Namibia secured a conservation financing agreement valued at over N$1 billion (approximately US$63 million). The initiative is designed to secure long-term funding for Namibia’s community-based conservation programme. The Government of the Republic of Namibia, together with communal conservancies and international partners, aims to secure the long-term conservation of more than 20 million hectares. The initiative brings together Namibia’s Ministry of Environment, Forestry and Tourism, CCFN, NACSO, WWF Namibia and the Impact Tank Analysis Foundation.This area covers over 20% of the country and is larger than Senegal. The initiative is described in the release as Africa’s first Project Finance for Permanence model designed to secure funding, policies and systems needed to sustain conservation over the long term. It builds on Namibia’s approach to community-based conservation.How will the programme support Namibia’s communal conservancies‘Namibia for Life’ currently supports 87 communal conservancies and is expected to expand to as many as 100 over time. The programme is expected to benefit more than 283,000 people who depend on wildlife and natural resources for their livelihoods. It aims to strengthen Namibia’s community-based conservation approach. It will support conservancies to maintain strong governance, improve natural resources management and expand economic opportunities for rural communities.Communities have played a central role in protecting wildlife and managing natural resources since the establishment of conservancies in 1998. The release links this approach with key species, including black rhino populations, which grew from only a few hundred in 1990 to around 2,000 today, alongside recoveries in elephant and desert-adapted lion populations.What role will the new funds play in supporting communitiesAt the centre of ‘Namibia for Life’ is a long-term financing approach that includes an endowment fund. The fund is intended to provide stable and predictable support beyond short-term projects. A dedicated Socio-Economic Development Fund will support community priorities by strengthening local enterprises, creating jobs, building skills and investing in small-scale infrastructure.The release says this structure is intended to ensure that conservation continues to deliver tangible economic value for rural communities. The Community Conservation Fund of Namibia will manage the financing mechanism. Continued technical support will help conservancies strengthen governance, financial management and conservation practices over time.‘Namibia for Life’ brings long-term funding to community conservation‘Namibia for Life’ is part of an effort supported through Enduring Earth, a collaboration working to secure long-term conservation financing worldwide. Since 2021, the programme has supported initiatives covering more than 231 million hectares globally and mobilised over US$1.8 billion in funding. In Namibia, the initiative is intended to strengthen community-led conservation while supporting livelihoods linked to wildlife and natural resources.A dedicated fund will help local enterprises, jobs, skills and small-scale infrastructure. The release also highlights the role of conservancies in managing wildlife and natural resources. The financing mechanism will be managed by CCFN, while technical support will focus on governance, financial management and conservation practices.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Hull Truck Theatre makes security centre stage after break-ins
articles.summary: Hull Truck wants to improve security after break-ins and robbery attempts.
articles.body:
A theatre is bidding for council funding to bolster its security after being hit by break-ins, thefts and antisocial behaviour.

A report due before Hull City Council's crime prevention grants sub-committee revealed that Hull Truck Theatre was targeted in three separate break-in and robbery attempts between October 2025 and March 2026.

In two cases, offenders succeeded in gaining access while audiences were watching performances and staff were at work, stealing both professional equipment and personal belongings.

The theatre said it had also faced regular problems with groups of teenagers entering the building without permission, taking items from the bar and intimidating staff.

According to the theatre, a recent security review identified three blind spots in the current CCTV system, which the theatre plans to address with new wide-angle cameras covering key access points.

The total cost of the improvements is £8,747, including £780 for CCTV upgrades and £7,967 for door improvements.

The additional measures would reduce opportunities for crime and improve public safety, the theatre said.

The funding bid was due to be heard by councillors on Monday.

articles.title: In 2000, Bruce Willis bought 7.3 acres on Parrot Cay; over four years he built three homes, four pools and a beachfront yoga pavilion before selling the Caribbean compound for $27 million in 2019
articles.summary: Bruce Willis has completed the sale of his beachfront retreat on Parrot Cay in Turks and Caicos for $27 million.
articles.body: Bruce Willis has completed the sale of his beachfront retreat on Parrot Cay in Turks and Caicos for $27 million. The deal is one of the highest property sales ever recorded in the Caribbean territory. Property records cited by the Los Angeles Times and Architectural Digest say the American actor bought the 7.3-acre site in 2000. Over the next four years, Willis turned the undeveloped land into a private compound with several homes. The property has more than 35,000 square feet of living space and decks.Four years of custom constructionWhen Willis bought the 7.3-acre site in 2000, there was nothing built on it. Architectural Digest reported that the actor spent four years managing the construction of three separate hardwood homes. The houses were built along 1,100 feet of white sand beach. The main home is the center of the compound. It has six bedrooms, high ceilings, exposed wood beams and large glass doors that open toward the ocean. Two separate guest villas sit beside the main house. Each has two bedrooms and was designed to give family and friends their own private space. Together, the three homes have 12 bedrooms and 14 bathrooms. They cover 13,500 square feet of interior living space. Covered verandas and outdoor decks add another large area, bringing the total usable living and deck space to more than 35,000 square feet.Amenities and outdoor featuresThe property was designed for outdoor fun, privacy and time with family. Each of the three homes has its own swimming pool. A fourth pool was built for children inside a fenced play area. Other buildings added during the four-year project include a beachfront yoga pavilion, a commercial-grade kitchen annex for full-service catering, and private quarters for staff. The grounds also have a paved children's playground with a life-sized pirate ship. "We fell in love with Turks and Caicos the moment we arrived," Willis and his wife, Emma Heming Willis, said in an official statement released through Sotheby's International Realty when the property was listed. "The island gave us complete privacy and allowed us to create a space where our family could gather and grow together." Willis and Emma Heming Willis renewed their wedding vows at the estate in March 2019, shortly before the property was put up for sale.Record valuation and market impactThe property was first listed for sale in March 2019 for $33 million, according to the Los Angeles Times. Turks & Caicos Sotheby's International Realty brokers Nina Siegenthaler and Joe Zavaglia handled the listing. Billionaire businessman Mark Ein, founder of Capitol Investment Corp., paid the final negotiated price of $27 million. The final price was $6 million below the original asking price. Still, the sale was the second-highest residential real estate transaction in Turks and Caicos history. The regional record remained with a nearby estate on Grace Bay, which sold for $32.5 million earlier that year.Island refuge for high-profile residentsParrot Cay is a private 1,000-acre island in the Turks and Caicos archipelago. It can only be reached by a 35-minute boat ride from the main island of Providenciales. Architectural Digest has reported that the island has long been a private retreat for wealthy residents because of its security and secluded location. The resort area, managed by COMO Hotels and Resorts, gives estate owners access to spa services, private dining and personal butler services. The sale of the Parrot Cay compound was part of a larger effort by Willis and his family to reduce and reorganize their real estate holdings. During the same period, the actor also sold several other properties, including an estate in Bedford, New York, and a ski chalet in Sun Valley, Idaho, as he moved his primary home to the West Coast.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Indian Green Card applicants see mysterious USCIS status change, immigration lawyer says it must be a 'system glitch'
articles.summary: Several Indian Green Card applicants reported an unexpected change in their status online which says their case \"requires USCIS to send a notice\".
articles.body: Several Indian Green Card applicants reported an unexpected change in their status online which says their case "requires USCIS to send a notice". Immigration attorney Rahul Reddy said this has led to a great deal of anxiety but this is most probably a glitch in the system and there is no real reason to panic. Reddy said most of the affected applicants are Indian nationals in the EB-2 and EB-3 categories and many have their priority dates from 2014 and 2015. Families waiting for their Green Cards for years are worried that something has gone wrong with their applications now but this might not be the case."When USCIS has a genuine concern about an individual application, it acts on that specific case. What we are seeing now is the same status message appearing across thousands of pending cases at the same time, regardless of priority date, filing date, or case history. Many of these applicants have final action dates that are not even current, which means USCIS cannot approve or deny their cases on the merits right now. A status change of this scale and uniformity reflects a system-level update, not a problem with your file," Reddy said.USCIS has not announced any change in processing of Green Cards that might have caused the status change, Reddy said urging Indian Green Card applicants to not pay heed to social media speculations."Continue to maintain your status, keep your employment and contact information up to date, and do not file anything with USCIS in response to this online message alone," Reddy said."If a physical notice does arrive in the mail, stay calm and read it carefully. Many notices are routine. If a notice asks for documents or sets a response deadline, share it with your attorney promptly so a timely and complete response can be prepared. Deadlines on USCIS notices are strict, and a missed deadline can cause real problems even when the underlying case is strong," Reddy added.Delay in October visa bulletinThe Department of State has not yet officially released the October 2026 visa bulletin. October marks the start of Fiscal Year 2027 when the annual employment-based and family-sponsored visa numbers will be reset.Legal consultant Bhumireddy Sai Srinivas Reddy said he believed that the visa bulletin has been delayed because of the reversal of the 75-country visa pause. "On August 21, Judge Vargas ruled that the 75-country visa freeze was illegal. She ordered the State Department to reconsider 43,000+ visa applications that were denied solely because of that freeze. But the government is fighting back. They asked Judge Vargas to pause her order while they appeal and gave her a deadline: September 25," he said."The State Department can't finalize the October bulletin without knowing what's going to happen to those 43,000 cases. If the appeals court pauses the order, the cases stay on hold visa numbers stay tight, priority dates move slowly. If the court rejects the pause, 43,000 cases flood into adjudication visa numbers expand, priority dates could jump. The State Department is literally waiting to know which scenario is happening before they can publish accurate cutoff dates," he said, adding that it was his personal analysis of the situation.You use AI every day. articles.title: Remains of dozens of kidnapping victims found in Nigerian forests
articles.summary: Investigations are ongoing to establish the identities of at least 28 people whose remains were recovered by police.
articles.body:
The skulls and bones of at least 28 people have been recovered from suspected criminal camps in Nigerian forests.

Police in the south-eastern state of Abia are investigating the identities of the remains found in the Umuaku and Nneato forests on Saturday after a security operation was carried out in the Umunneochi area.

Police spokeswoman Maureen Chinaka said the suspects fled when police arrived.

The discovery is likely to revive concerns about kidnapping gangs operating in remote forests across parts of south-eastern Nigeria, where criminal groups have frequently targeted motorists, travellers and residents for ransom.

According to Abia State Police Command, the raids were launched following intelligence reports about suspected criminal activity in the forests.

Officers suspect the remains belong to kidnapping victims, although forensic and other investigations are ongoing to establish their identities and the circumstances surrounding their deaths.

"Upon arrival of the Command's tactical operatives at the camps, the suspects fled. The criminal camps were subsequently dismantled. A total of twenty-eight human skulls and bones, suspected to be kidnap victims, were recovered," Chinaka said in a statement.

Police said surveillance had been intensified in the area as officers sought to track down those who fled.

Abia state police commissioner Wilfred Afolabi said the operation was part of an ongoing campaign to dismantle criminal hideouts in the state.

Police have appealed to residents to report suspicious activity and security concerns as efforts continue to identify the victims and determine whether the remains are connected to unresolved kidnapping cases in the region.

Authorities have previously discovered decomposing bodies believed to be linked to kidnapping activities during security raids in Umunneochi .

Separately over the weekend, more than 80 people, mostly women, were seized in separate mass kidnappings in two states in the country's north.

In an attack on Sunday, nearly 50 farmers were abducted by gunmen in Niger State.

On Sunday, about 40 other women were kidnapped in the neighbouring state of Zamfara, according to two security reports seen by AFP and a local source.

Abductions for ransom have become a key source of income for criminals, including bandits and militant Islamists, in northern Nigeria.

articles.title: UK needs plan in case of 'unprecedented' AI job losses, says minister
articles.summary: Kanishka Narayan says one of his top priorities is to have a plan in place if job losses are as bad as some fear.
articles.body:
The government must "take seriously the possibility of an unprecedented impact on the jobs market" caused by artificial intelligence (AI), a UK minister has said.

AI Minister Kanishka Narayan said there was no evidence so far of an overall reduction in jobs as a result of AI, but one of his priorities was to have a contingency plan in place for worst case scenarios.

"If it's going to hit us in a big way, you are going to want to be as ahead of the curve as possible," he told a fringe meeting at the Labour Party conference.

Carsten Jung, of the IPPR think tank, said: "In a worst case scenario you could have about 8 million jobs being negatively affected by this."

Jung said the think tank was working on a "pandemic preparedness" report on AI labour market disruption.

The level of AI adoption by industry was not that high so far and it might not ultimately lead to massive job losses, he said, but he claimed it was still going to have a bigger impact on the labour market than the industrial revolution.

He also admitted that "stark scenarios" the IPPR had produced in 2024 were "to some extent" wrong but, he argued, AI had evolved rapidly since then from doing "boring" tasks to "more high-level reasoning and creative tasks".

"We are not preparing enough for something quite big that's coming," he told the meeting.

According to Jung, about 11% of UK jobs are "highly exposed" to being replaced by AI chatbots, "led by secretarial and administrative occupations".

But with the rise of more sophisticated agentic AI, he argued that the proportion "could rise to about 60% of tasks across the UK economy".

The government needed to be ready to help retrain service sector workers, he argued, but also to bring in measures to "slow down the transition slightly" to keep people in their jobs.

That could involve redesigning tax structures to "make it a bit more attractive to hold on to workers than automating them," he said.

But he warned that "a lot of the policies we might want to do in a really severe disruption scenario will cost a lot of money," particularly as the UK is more of a service-based economy than other G7 nations.

He also said that women were "40% more exposed than men" to the threat of AI because a higher proportion worked in service jobs.

Narayan told the meeting that the impact of AI might have been under-estimated because of the "silent adoption" of the technology by workers, which did not show up in industry surveys.

UK firms had said there was "no aggregate impact in the overall labour market today," the AI minister added, but one tech firm had told him they had hired fewer people because tasks had been automated "so the actual net impact might not be fully captured".

The minister said he was determined that workers would have a voice in the transition to AI, and promised "much better transparency when AI and technology is adopted" so that any productivity gains could be measured.

And he said one of his top priorities was "thinking through what you would do in contingency" if the job losses were as bad as some were predicting.

This could involve changes to "labour market policy" and "even where we might go on some aspects of regulation," he added.

Mike Clancy, general secretary of the Prospect trade union, welcomed the government's commitment to giving workers more of a say, but warned against "creating the conditions in which working people become victims" of AI.

Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has, meanwhile, used his conference speech to fire a warning shot at "tech titans" he said could not be relied on to manage the safety risks posed by AI alone.

He said that while some tech companies were "calling for us to act", others "are saying we should leave it all to them".

But he argued that the "lesson of history is that we cannot leave it to corporations to put in place the guardrails to serve the public interest".

"It is neither their purpose nor their motive, theirs is to maximise profits. We cannot and will not allow that to come at the expense of our children or indeed humanity," he continued.

He said that while the "technological progress" from AI was "inspiring", the "threat it poses according to its own inventors is daunting".

He said the UK would confront those "urgent risks", including by using its G20 presidency next year to "lead the efforts to manage AI so we keep our country and our world safe".

articles.title: Trump officials warn China is weaponizing rare-earth dominance as Beijing uses critical minerals for leverage
articles.summary: David Perdue says China has "weaponized" rare earths dominance, warning that U.S. supply chains face risks including arrest and asset seizures.
articles.body: U.S. Ambassador to China David Perdue is warning that Beijing has "weaponized" its dominance over critical minerals, saying China has expanded its rules to the point that efforts to diversify supply chains away from the country could expose people to arrest, criminal prosecution and asset seizures. "This is a single-source dominant position that China is weaponizing against the world right now," Perdue told "Fox News Sunday." "We have committed to them that this is unacceptable." GOV MIKE DUNLEAVY: CHINA IS HOLDING CRITICAL MINERALS HOSTAGE. ALASKA CAN HELP END THE THREAT Perdue pledged that the U.S. will not kowtow to China to do business, arguing that America's dependence on Beijing for critical materials has been decades in the making. "Twenty years ago, the United States had single-source dominant positions in rare earth magnets, commercial shipbuilding [and] pharmaceuticals," Perdue added. "And all these have been absconded by China in a way that we allowed over the last 20 years." Now, he said, the Trump administration is seeking to reverse that dependence and rebuild America's ability to operate without relying on Beijing. We're going to be independent.’" Perdue's warning comes as U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer separately raised concerns about China's rare-earth deliveries, saying the U.S. wants the critical materials in "greater volumes" and in a "more timely way." "That's something that we continue [to] work on. President Trump raised it with President Xi quite directly, and that's just one of many items that we're still looking at," he told Fox News' Jacqui Heinrich. articles.title: UK to reopen refugee resettlement scheme as home secretary Shabana Mahmood promises capped, controlled routes
articles.summary: UK Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has announced the reopening of the refugee resettlement scheme to provide legal pathways for refugees and control illegal Channel crossings. This initiative aims to support Afghan women, girls, and Palestinians, while establishing capped routes for resettlement.
articles.body: UK Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has announced the reopening of the country’s refugee resettlement scheme, expanding legal pathways for people fleeing conflict while seeking to reduce dangerous Channel crossings.The UK Resettlement Scheme (UKRS) will reopen immediately, with Afghan women and girls and Palestinians expected to account for about a quarter of arrivals, the Home Office said. The government expects hundreds of refugees to arrive initially, with numbers potentially reaching the low thousands as illegal migration falls.The scheme stopped accepting new applicants in December 2024. Alongside its reopening, the government is introducing three sponsorship routes involving communities, universities and employers, with the first arrivals under the new routes expected from 2027.Speaking at the Labour Party conference on Monday, Mahmood said the state had a responsibility to help people fleeing war and persecution but stressed that the system must remain limited.“We must live up to our international obligations,” she said, while stressing that refugee routes needed to be “capped and controlled”.An annual limit will apply to the routes, although the government has not yet announced the number of people who will be accepted.Those arriving through the safe and legal pathways will be placed on a five-year route towards permanent settlement, according to the plans.Mahmood said the approach was intended to combine greater control over Britain's borders with legal alternatives for refugees.“That is what we can do, this is who we can be, as we restore control to our borders, bear down on small boat crossings and unlock the inherent generosity of this country,” she said.The government has linked the expansion of legal routes to its wider efforts to tackle irregular migration. More than 18,500 people have crossed the English Channel in small boats so far this year, compared with more than 32,000 during the same period in 2025.The announcement has drawn criticism from the Conservatives. Shadow home secretary Chris Philp accused Mahmood of making a “desperate attempt to appease” Labour members who have opposed parts of her asylum reforms.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Maryland couple bought 116 acres as a hunting property; 20 years later, they had replaced crops with native grasses, wildflowers and trees and permanently protected the land for wildlife
articles.summary: When Louise and John Durocher bought 116 acres in Kent County, Maryland, the property was intended primarily as a hunting retreat.
articles.body: When Louise and John Durocher bought 116 acres in Kent County, Maryland, the property was intended primarily as a hunting retreat. Over the next two decades, however, the couple gradually changed its purpose. They stopped growing crops and began restoring the fields with native grasses, wildflowers, shrubs and trees. They planted river birch, tulip poplar, sycamore, white oak, loblolly pine, black walnut and pawpaw, creating a mosaic of meadows, woodland, wetlands and hedgerows. Now known as Tavern Creek Farm, the property has been placed under a permanent conservation easement through the Eastern Shore Land Conservancy and the Durocher family. Eastern Shore Undercover reports that the agreement will protect the land from future development and preserve its value as wildlife habitat, while safeguarding water quality in Tavern Creek and the Chesapeake Bay. Read on to know more:A hunting property with a different futureWhen Louise and John Durocher purchased the 116-acre farm, they imagined using it as a hunting property.The land still contained fields that had been used for growing crops. It was productive farmland, but the couple gradually began to see possibilities beyond cultivation.About 20 years ago, they stopped farming crops on the property and started converting the fields into habitat. Instead of leaving the land bare or allowing it to become dominated by invasive plants, they planted native grasses, wildflowers, shrubs and trees.The change was gradual. A field does not become mature habitat in one season. Grasses need time to establish, trees must grow and wildlife begins using the land at different stages of recovery.The Durochers continued the process over many years, creating a landscape that combined open meadows, forest, wetlands, hedgerows and water. Their original hunting property became a long-term restoration project.Today, Tavern Creek Farm is protected from future development through a permanent conservation easement.The first field of wildflowersOne of the couple’s earliest signs of success came after they planted wildflowers.Louise Durocher recalled that coreopsis covered about five acres in gold during the first year the wildflower planting bloomed.That image captures the appeal of habitat restoration. A field that once supported crops can become a living display of native colour and seasonal change.Wildflowers provide nectar and pollen for bees, butterflies and other insects. Their seeds can feed birds and small mammals, while their roots help hold soil in place and improve its structure.Unlike a uniform crop field, a meadow can contain many plant species with different heights, flowering periods and root systems. That diversity creates more shelter and food for wildlife throughout the year.The golden coreopsis also offered a visible sign that the Durochers’ choices were working. The property was not simply being left alone. It was developing into a more varied and biologically active landscape.Planting a native woodlandThe family planted a wide range of trees across the farm.The restoration included river birch, tulip poplar, sycamore, white oak, loblolly pine, black walnut and pawpaw. Each species contributes different qualities to the developing woodland.River birch can thrive near water, while white oaks provide acorns that support wildlife. Tulip poplars grow tall and can eventually form part of the forest canopy. Pawpaws produce fruit, and black walnuts contribute both habitat and food value.Planting different species reduces reliance on a single type of tree. A diverse woodland is generally better able to withstand pests, disease, storms and changing environmental conditions.The trees also create a transition between open fields and older forest. As they mature, they provide nesting sites, shade and cover while connecting separate habitats.The work will continue beyond the Durochers’ lifetime. Trees planted today may reach their greatest ecological value decades from now, which is one reason permanent protection is so important.Meadows connected by hedgerowsTavern Creek Farm contains open meadows of warm-season and cool-season grasses. These meadows are connected to woodland through long hedgerows.Hedgerows can act as wildlife corridors. They provide shelter for animals moving between fields, forest and water, while offering nesting sites and food for birds and insects.A continuous hedgerow can be especially valuable in a rural landscape where open fields might otherwise leave animals exposed. Small mammals can travel under cover, birds can forage along the edge and pollinators can move between flowering plants.The contrast between meadow and forest also increases habitat diversity. Some species prefer open grassland, while others depend on dense shrubs or mature trees.The farm’s restoration created several habitat types close together. That arrangement makes the property more useful to wildlife than a single uniform landscape.It also gives the land a more natural appearance. Instead of large fields separated only by fences or roads, the property now contains layers of vegetation that follow its watercourses and contours.Wetlands that hold waterThe farm includes approximately 26 acres of wetlands.Wetlands are among the most valuable natural features on the property because they can retain stormwater, support wildlife and help cycle nutrients. Eastern Shore Land Conservancy President and CEO Steve Kline said the wetlands provide stormwater retention and nutrient cycling benefits, as per the report.During heavy rainfall, wetlands can temporarily hold water and reduce the speed at which it moves across the landscape. This can help limit erosion and reduce the amount of sediment reaching streams.Wetland plants can also absorb or process nutrients. That function is important in the Chesapeake Bay watershed, where excess nitrogen and phosphorus can contribute to algae growth and oxygen depletion.Wetlands provide breeding and feeding habitat for amphibians, insects, birds and other animals. They also create conditions that differ from dry meadows and upland woodland.Protecting the wetlands therefore benefits both local wildlife and downstream water quality. The value of the farm extends beyond its boundaries because water leaving the property eventually reaches larger waterways.Protecting Tavern Creek and the Chesapeake BayThe Durochers hoped to conserve the property partly because of its connection to the Chesapeake Bay.Louise said she had a long association with the Chesapeake and had always hoped to protect the farm in a way that would help safeguard the Bay.Tavern Creek is an important part of that connection. The property contains woodland along the creek and includes more than 9,000 feet of creek frontage.The farm also has about 24 acres of woodland running along its length. Along with tree plantings and more than 18 acres of conservation cover, the woodland helps protect water quality in Tavern Creek and the farm’s ponds.Trees and vegetation along streams can reduce runoff, stabilise stream banks and filter sediment before it enters the water. Their roots hold soil in place, while fallen leaves and woody debris contribute to aquatic ecosystems.These functions make the farm part of a wider watershed protection effort. Conservation on one property may not solve all Chesapeake Bay problems, but many protected properties together can improve the health of the entire system.Wildlife already using the landThe restored habitats support a variety of wildlife.The conservation report mentions beavers, otters, opossums and muskrats, along with many types of birds. These animals use different parts of the property, including wetlands, waterways, grasslands, hedgerows and woodland.Beavers can alter water flow and create wet habitat, while otters depend on healthy waterways and sufficient prey. Opossums and muskrats use vegetation and wetland edges for food and shelter.Birds benefit from the range of habitat types. Grassland birds can use the meadows, woodland species can nest in trees and shrubs can provide cover for migrating birds.The property also includes an osprey stand, which has become part of the family’s experience of the land. Ospreys depend on open water and suitable nesting structures, making their presence a sign of the importance of the creek and surrounding habitat.As restoration continues, wildlife use may increase or change. Some species will benefit from young vegetation, while others may arrive as trees mature and wetlands develop.More than a decade of conservation practicesMore than 31 acres of the farm, including nearly all of its shoreline, have been enrolled in Farm Bill conservation practices for more than a decade.The federal conservation programmes encourage landowners to establish or maintain habitat, protect wetlands and reduce environmental impacts from agriculture.Those practices provided a foundation for the broader restoration. The family was not starting from zero when the conservation easement was created. Much of the land had already been managed with wildlife and water quality in mind.The permanent easement now adds another layer of protection. Conservation practices can be changed or renewed over time, while an easement creates a lasting legal limit on development.Together, the two approaches help ensure that Tavern Creek Farm remains a connected natural landscape. The property can continue to be managed, but its core conservation values cannot be replaced by houses, commercial buildings or intensive development.What a conservation easement doesA conservation easement is a legal agreement that permanently restricts certain uses of private land.The land remains privately owned, but development rights are limited. The agreement can protect forests, wetlands, streams, open fields and wildlife habitat even if ownership changes in the future.In Tavern Creek Farm’s case, the easement was created through a partnership between the Eastern Shore Land Conservancy and the Durocher family. Funding came from the United States Department of Agriculture and Maryland’s Conservation Reserve Enhancement Permanent Easement Program, also known as CREP.The agreement means the 116 acres will remain wild and natural rather than being converted to developed uses.That does not necessarily mean the family cannot visit, fish, kayak, pick fruit or maintain parts of the property. The family hopes future generations can continue enjoying the land while caring for its woodlands, wetlands and grasslands.Conservation easements are designed to balance private ownership with long-term public benefits. They keep land in family hands while protecting ecological features that benefit the broader community.A family legacy continuesThe property is now cared for by Sarah Starman, the granddaughter of Louise and John Durocher.Starman said it was rewarding to see the farm become more beautiful and biodiverse because of her grandparents’ work and the family’s continued efforts. She added that knowing the land would always be protected gave her security and motivation to continue caring for it.Her comments show how conservation can pass from one generation to another.The Durochers began the restoration by changing the land’s use. Starman now has the responsibility of maintaining and building on that work.The permanent easement provides reassurance that future owners will not be able to undo the entire project through development. It also creates a clear framework for stewardship.Over time, the property may become even more diverse. Trees will mature, meadow plants will spread and wildlife populations may change with the seasons.The family’s role is not finished when the easement is signed. Permanent protection ensures the opportunity to continue caring for the land.A place for family lifeTavern Creek Farm is not only a conservation project. It is also a place where the family lives and spends time.Starman hopes future generations will enjoy kayaking and fishing in Tavern Creek, watching ospreys, picking blueberries in spring, gathering figs in summer and having barbecues near the house.These activities connect conservation with everyday life.A protected landscape does not have to be separated from human enjoyment. People can experience nature while respecting wildlife and maintaining the habitats that make those experiences possible.Fishing and kayaking can help family members understand the creek as a living system. Picking fruit and walking through meadows can make seasonal changes more visible. Caring for the woods and wetlands turns conservation into a shared responsibility rather than an abstract goal.The family’s vision is for future residents to enjoy the same peace while continuing to maintain the property as wildlife habitat.A quiet transformationThe story of Tavern Creek Farm is not about a sudden rewilding project.It is about decisions made over 20 years. The Durochers stopped farming crops, planted native species, maintained conservation practices and allowed the land to develop into a more complex habitat.The transformation happened gradually. A meadow that once looked like an ordinary field became a place for wildflowers and grasses. Tree plantings became hedgerows and woodland. Wetlands and creek edges gained greater protection.The result is a landscape where agriculture, family life and wildlife conservation overlap.The permanent easement now ensures that this transformation will not be reversed by future development. The 116 acres will remain connected to Tavern Creek, its wetlands and the wildlife that depends on them.Tavern Creek Farm shows how private landowners can improve a landscape without waiting for a large public project. A decision made for a hunting property became a long-term commitment to biodiversity and clean water.For the Durocher family, protecting the farm means preserving both a place they love and a natural legacy that can continue for generations.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Andrew Bailey resigns from his role as FBI Co-Deputy Director after a year, citing a desire to return to his family in Missouri. His departure comes amid ongoing investigations related to the 2020 election.
articles.body: FBI Co-Deputy Director Andrew Bailey is stepping down from his post after just over a year at the US law enforcement agency, saying he is leaving to return to his family in Missouri.Bailey, a Republican ally of President Donald Trump, announced his resignation on Monday after joining the FBI from his position as Missouri attorney general. He served under FBI Director Kash Patel and was involved in investigations related to the 2020 US election.Writing on X (formerly Twitter), Bailey thanked Trump, Attorney General Todd Blanche and Patel for the opportunity to serve at the FBI.“With great pride in what we have accomplished, I am announcing that I am stepping down to return to my family in Missouri,” Bailey wrote.He also expressed support for Patel, “I am confident Director Patel will continue to reform the FBI, combat violent crime, defend the homeland, ensure strong organizational accountability, and restore public trust in this institution of excellence.”Bailey was part of the FBI leadership overseeing day-to-day law enforcement operations. During his tenure, he helped manage the Trump administration's investigations into election-related issues and was present when FBI agents seized 2020 election ballots in Georgia earlier this year.The FBI has examined election records in several states but has not produced evidence supporting Trump's claims that widespread voter fraud caused his defeat in the 2020 presidential election.Bailey's departure comes about five weeks before the US midterm elections, which will determine control of Congress. The Trump administration has also stepped up federal investigations into voting by non-US citizens ahead of the elections.The FBI's deputy director position has traditionally been held by career bureau officials and was considered a non-political role. Under Trump, political allies have been appointed to senior positions as the administration seeks to reshape the agency.Bailey initially served as co-deputy director alongside Dan Bongino, a former US Secret Service agent and conservative podcaster. Bongino left the FBI in January.He joined the FBI amid scrutiny of Patel's leadership, including the bureau's handling of investigative files involving late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, which created political pressure for the Trump administration and tensions within the Justice Department.Bailey did not give a reason for his departure beyond his decision to return to his family.You use AI every day. articles.title: Aldi boss says some of rivals' loyalty discounts 'dupe' customers
articles.summary: Aldi is the only major supermarket chain that doesn't operate a loyalty scheme, which are hugely popular and used by millions of shoppers.
articles.body:
Aldi's UK boss has accused rival supermarket chains of duping customers in some cases with loyalty discounts that start with "unrealistically high prices" and then drop.

Chief executive Giles Hurley said discounts are helpful "when they're real and when they show realistic reductions", but hit out at what he said were unrealistic reductions which "dupe customers".

Aldi is the only major supermarket chain that doesn't operate a loyalty scheme, which are used by millions of shoppers.

The UK's official competition watchdog investigated supermarkets' loyalty pricing schemes in 2024 and concluded shoppers "almost always make a genuine saving".

Former Asda buyer and retail consultant Ged Futter told the BBC Hurley's comments were a "a distraction from the fact is that Aldi is under pressure in the UK".

He said Aldi was "on a meteoric rise until about two years ago" but that it is "now growing behind the main supermarket pack".

"The price gap isn't as clear as it once was," he added.

Hurley, who has made similar comments on discount schemes in the past, was speaking as Aldi reported a 5% increase in sales to £19bn for 2025 from 2024.

However, operating profits had fallen slightly over the same period, which the retailer said was due to higher staff pay as well as investments in infrastructure and prices.

Hurley said the business was attracting new customers despite fierce competition across the sector.

"We are the only retailer where the price of your weekly shop is actually cheaper this summer than last summer," said Hurley

He said the business was focussed on "everyday low prices, not short-lived offers that disappear the following week".

"Promotions can supplement every day low prices when they're meaningful, when they're real and when they show realistic reductions.

"However, when promotions start with unrealistically high prices – and come down to prices which aren't that competitive and dupe customers – we would view that as loyalty that isn't supportive, that isn't transparent and doesn't help customers plan and budget."

Aldi said it had spent £340m this year on cutting prices. The German-owned chain also announced plans to open 40 new stores next year as part of a £900m investment programme and expand long-term agreements with British suppliers.

Hurley said recent droughts and global events had highlighted vulnerabilities in food supply chains, arguing that boosting domestic production should be a national strategic priority, helping to reduce the UK's exposure to shocks that can push up food prices.

articles.title: Turkey stand-up comic released after being convicted of insulting Erdoğan
articles.summary: Turkish comedian Deniz Göktaş also faces a travel ban but has been released due to time served.
articles.body:
An Istanbul court has convicted a popular comedian of insulting President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan – and handed down a sentence of almost 19 months – but ordered his release due to time served.

It has also placed him under a travel ban, preventing him from travelling outside Turkey.

A final decision in the case will come from the court of appeals.

Deniz Göktaş - who denied the charges - has already spent nearly 90 days in prison. Prosecutors had asked for up to 12 years. His case comes amid a wave of arrests in Turkey that human rights groups say is aimed at crushing dissent.

His stand-up routine went viral on YouTube, attracting more than 15 million views.

Prosecutors had singled out a line in which the comedian called the Turkish leader "a shy dictator", but Göktaş insisted there was "no criminal element" in his comments.

"Dictator is not an insult," he said, "it is a political characterisation."

But angering the president in Turkey is not funny. Göktaş was arrested and handcuffed at Istanbul airport in July when he returned from a holiday.

During his court appearance on Monday, it was clear he did not lose his sense of humour during his 88 days in solitary confinement.

"Three months have been taken away from my life," he said on the stand. "But I quit smoking, so I'll add another three months to my life." That drew laughter and loud applause in court.

Outside, supporters like Firat Aksal – a fellow comedian – were very pleasantly surprised by the verdict.

"We hardly know what to do with our happiness," he said. "We are thrilled. To be honest we weren't hopeful of getting a fair trial. "

Göktaş was released at 21:45 local time (18:45 GMT) and greeted by well-wishers, including his parents who he was seen hugging, outside a prison facility.

Aksal said Göktaş would now rest for a few days, and see his family, and then return to the stage.

After his release, Göktaş told reporters: "I'm very happy to be reunited with my family, mother, father, and friends."

But he added: "There are thousands of other people in prisons across Turkey. Some, like me, are being held in pre-trial detention, while others have been convicted because of their views.

"So, of course, it's wonderful to be out. I've missed it very much. But there is not much difference between inside and outside. I hope the day comes when we can all regain our freedom together."

Many others remain behind bars, including journalists, human rights campaigners, student protesters, LGBTQ activists, and the elected Mayor of Istanbul, Ekrem Imamoglu. Prisons are full in Turkey these days.

Erdogan and his party in the past have denied arrests, such as that of Imamoglu, have been politically motivated , insisting that Turkey's judiciary is independent.

articles.title: 'Wizards of Waverly Place' star David Henrie says his faith cost him agents, money and friends in Hollywood
articles.summary: David Henrie revealed on a podcast that committing to his Catholic faith cost him agents, friends and money, but said he found new friends and opportunities along the way.
articles.body: David Henrie, best known for his role in "Wizards of Waverly Place," revealed during a September podcast interview that he lost friends and jobs after committing to his faith. During an appearance on the "Bryce Crawford Podcast," Henrie was asked what his faith cost him in Hollywood. "It was rough, lost my agents," he said. "I walked away from a lot. I turned down a lot of roles. I was like I'm just not going to do something that I think will disrespect my belief now or disrespect our Lord. I'm just not going to do it. I'm not going to go near it. And it cost me a lot. It cost a lot. I lost a lot of money. Friends, a girlfriend at the time. I kind of was stripped of everyone, everyone that I would call a friend." However, Henrie added that he made new friends that challenged him, which eventually led to him meeting his wife. FORMER DISNEY STAR DAVID HENRIE REJECTED 'SECULAR' HOLLYWOOD LIFESTYLE AFTER LIFE-CHANGING MONASTERY VISIT "I found new friends," he said. "I found guys I respected, guys I loved, that were building me up in Christ. You know, I think that friendship is like an elevator. It brings you up or it brings you down. So, I made new friends and I made friends that elevated me and that challenged me, gave me great books to read and helped form me in my faith and led to meeting my wife, my best friend now." Henrie said it had been a "great journey" and that some of the people he lost had come back into the picture. "Some of those people who left have now come back into the picture," he said. "They've gotten older. They've changed the way that they think. And I get texts from people like, 'Hey, just want you to know I went to church this Sunday.' And I was like, 'Oh, no way.' I didn't, would have never thought this person would, that would happen. And yeah, it's a marathon. It's not a race." Henrie told Fox News Digital in January that the industry was now much more accepting of faith. FROM DISNEY MAGIC TO ANCIENT FAITH: DAVID HENRIE ON WHY GEN Z IS FLOCKING TO CHURCH "Now people are much more accepting about people of faith," Henrie, who is a devout Catholic, told Fox News Digital, describing what he sees as a noticeable change from a decade ago. He said he regularly hears executives asking for "content for people of faith" because they’re "underrepresented" on screen. Henrie’s push for value-driven storytelling has become more personal since becoming a father, he said, shaping the kinds of projects he wants to champion and the kind of content he wants available for families like his. "I really wanted to find a way to use everything God’s given me to tell stories on a bigger scale," he said, explaining why he launched Novo Inspire Studios, a production company he describes as focused on "entertaining and elevating content." MARY J BLIGE CREDITS FAITH, PASTORS WITH CONFRONTING HER PRIDE AS SHE TOOK CONTROL OF HER CAREER Entrepreneur David Friedman, the head of Friedman Ventures, who has a Master's degree in philosophical theology, told Fox News Digital, "Mr. Henrie's comments reveal the natural implications of walking out your Christian faith in a cultural context that has opposing values and worldviews. What's not discussed is that the losses were due to fundamentally different understandings about what human flourishing really means." "However, there are many actors that also lose opportunities in staying true to their own versions of what is important," he continued. "The reality is that anyone that has a strong core faith or values will experience some form of rejection or cost, especially if the reigning paradigm is in direct opposition about the fundamental elements of reality, around morality and even the spiritual dimension to reality." Friedman pointed to Eric Liddell, the Scottish Olympian who chose not to run in a race in the 1924 Summer Olympics because the event was held on Sunday and conflicted with Sabbath. "The lesson applies to David and anyone in these situations, as the characters reveal that paradox of these tensions in that if Eric had run on Sunday, he would have cut himself off from the very power source that enabled him to win. That is the key for actors and anyone whose faith is central. There is really not another choice in these situations," Friedman continued. Entertainment journalist DeWayne Hamby said in a statement to Fox News Digital that Hollywood decision makers were likely a little scared of someone marching to the beat of a different drum. "I think it scares people a little bit, people who are making the decisions, that you have someone who you really can't predict," he said, responding to Henrie's comments about job loss. "They're marching to the beat of a different drummer, so they can't really predict them as much." FORMER DISNEY STAR JENNIFER STONE FOUND A LIFELINE IN THE ER AS FELLOW CHILD ACTORS SPIRALED Actor Chris Pratt said during an interview in March that success in the industry can quickly turn destructive without a strong inner foundation. "You are a man of great faith, and your Instagram bio says, ‘God first, grateful to be here.’ How has that guided you through your journey in Hollywood, a place not always known for its faith?" Craig Melvin asked Pratt on the "Today" show on March 17. "It is what it is, man. I got a belief and I go with it, and for the most part, it’s been amazing," Pratt answered. "I think, you know — there’s this Christine Caine quote that says, ‘If the light that shines upon you is greater than the light that’s within you, then the light that shines upon you will kill you.' And you see it in our business, man. You see people who have the world by the balls, and they just are so unhappy. Excuse my language." articles.title: UNFPA report: Migrant workers cite livelihood insecurity, low wages, poverty and debt as reasons for moving out for better life
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Nearly 72% of migrant workers surveyed in three south Indian states felt that moving for work has improved their standard of living and more
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Nearly 72% of migrant workers surveyed in three south Indian states felt that moving for work has improved their standard of living and more than half (around 57%) intended to continue working in their destination state, as per a new report.At the same time, it turns out that over 86% of workers have no signed employment contracts and many face difficulties ranging from accessing welfare and essential services to experiencing language, communication and social barriers.Clearly migration decisions are shaped strongly by livelihood insecurity and limited employment opportunities. Migrants cited low wages at origin, lack of jobs, better opportunities, irregular employment, poverty and debt among the principal reasons for moving.These findings are part of the South India Interstate Migration Survey (SIIMS) 2026, that offers first-of-its-kind data on the changing nature of migration within India and on how migrant workers from other states (primarily from northern and eastern) live and work in Karnataka, Keralam and Tamil Nadu.The study surveyed 1,824 migrant workers and covered sectors including agriculture, fishing and marine work, and daily labour in all three states. It also covered hospitality in Keralam, textile and garment work in Tamil Nadu, and scrap collection in Karnataka.Over 92% of the migrants came from West Bengal (26.2%), Bihar (21.8%), Assam (17.1%), Odisha (12%), UP (9.6%) and Jharkhand (5.6%).Conducted by the International Institute of Migration and Development (IIMAD), the study was supported by the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) in collaboration with the International Organization for Migration (IOM).It comes through that over 77% of the surveyed workers were recruited through non-contractor channels, nearly 58% are paid in cash with Rs 17640 the average monthly wage and the average working day being 9.87 hours. The report also brings into focus the gender disparity as it came through that women workers earned about Rs 3,313 less per month than men.The data shows that just a little over 19% of migrant workers can easily use their welfare benefits when they move between states; 35% can do so partly and around 45% can barely do so.It also comes through that over 73% face problems accessing welfare and 69% face problems accessing healthcare.The survey found that while 88.2% of migrant workers are included in formal financial services, exclusion was higher in Karnataka (26.8%) and among scrap collection workers (31.3%).The study recommends building on One Nation One Ration Card so that welfare benefits follow the worker, multilingual help desks and helplines, stronger labour inspection and closer coordination between states.Andrea M Wojnar, UNFPA India Representative and Country Director Bhutan said, “By highlighting critical gaps in welfare portability, healthcare access, and workplace protections, this study provides a clear roadmap for stakeholders to turn data into targeted action.”Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Day after, no class at SRFTI, cop cover for campus, 4 FIRs
articles.summary: SRFTI Kolkata tense after student-ABGP clash injures 30; police file 4 FIRs, probe CCTV, form fact-finding panel; ABGP plans consumer case; protests continue.
articles.body: Kolkata: The situation at Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute (SRFTI) remained tense on Monday, with police deployed outside the gates and students staging silent protests inside. No classes were held.Police registered four cases for Sunday’s violence, three naming unidentified SRFTI students and one naming the RSS-backed Akhil Bharatiya Grahak Panchayat (ABGP), which had booked an auditorium on the campus for an event. The clash between the students and ABGP members had left 30 students and two faculty members injured.One of the four FIRs, filed on a complaint by the additional OC of Panchasayar police station, alleges students wrongfully restrained police personnel on duty, used criminal force to deter public servants and vandalised a police vehicle. Lalbazar seniors said they have collected CCTV footage and have zeroed in on several persons for questioning. Cops on Monday recorded statements of six persons, including two students and staffers.Inside SRFTI, multiple meetings were held between the students and administration to de-escalate the situation. A fact-finding committee comprising faculty members was set up to establish the chronology of events on Sunday leading to the violence, enhance campus security and ensure safety of students and faculty.SRFTI students’ union president Blossom Hazarika told TOI they met director Santosh Ajmera and requested him to open the guest house for students who live outside the campus but he did not agree. “He asked us to remove the protest posters and stop writing on the walls. Basically, he was asking us not to protest anymore. Students did not agree and gheraoed his office after the meeting,” Hazarika said.The students also insisted that those responsible for renting out the main theatre to organisations unrelated to films be held accountable. “We want campus bylaws to be re-evaluated so that institute spaces are restricted strictly to film-related activities,” said Anamika Pal, a 17th batch student.The student councils of Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Pune, FTII Itanagar and Roopkala Kendra, a Kolkata-based govt-run film institute, expressed solidarity with the students of SRFTI on Monday.Stepping up the ante, Anjan Sinha of ABGP, which had booked the auditorium for a consumer awareness programme, told TOI the organisation will file a move consumer court against the film school. “We will file a consumer case against SRFTI for not giving us the service we paid for. We have already filed a complaint against accused persons who are so-called students. We have sufficient videos and photos to proceed with our complaint. We are also collecting details of injuries to our members and losses we suffered,” he said. “Why were they shouting ‘azaadi’ slogans? Why did they have to chant ‘Jai Bhim’? Some of the students seemed intoxicated,” he alleged.An SRFTI faculty member said they had advised the students to remain calm. Several of them also questioned the need to rent out the main theatre to an organisation with no connection to filmmaking. However, sources on campus claimed this practice was not new. “The main theatre has previously been given out on rent to banks to host their events,” a senior SRFTI faculty member explained.SRFTI Alumni Association, through its president Ranjit Bahadur and vice-president Anirban Dutta, strongly condemned the attack on students, detailing how they were “hunted down, chased, mobbed, and beaten” during a “cowardly barrage of stone-pelting and government property vandalism by outside forces”.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news.
